Formatting belongs to the formatter.\\n\\n===== /Users/yuratestdev/.claude/plugins/cache/evolve/evolve-skills/0.1.0/skills/code-standards/reference/universal.md =====\\n# The universal quality bar\\n\\nLanguage-agnostic; read alongside the file for the language you are in. §0 is the floor and holds in every file. §1 onward are the defaults for new code and the vocabulary for reviewing existing code — subordinate, for *style*, to rung 1 of the ladder in [`SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md), and never a licence to restyle a file you were only meant to fix.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 0. The floor\\n\\nThese hold regardless of what the surrounding file does. A file that violates one on every other line gets one fewer violation, not one more. Rung 1 governs style; it cannot lower this.\\n\\n1. **Every public signature is typed** — parameters and return, in every language that can express it.\\n2. **No error is swallowed.** No empty `catch`, bare `except:`, `_ = err`, discarded exit code. An ignorable failure is logged, and a comment says why it is ignorable.\\n3. **No escape hatch outside tests without a comment saying why** — `any`, `as`/`!` to silence a type error, `!!`, `unwrap()`/`expect()`, `unsafe`, `# type: ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `#[allow]`. In tests, an unwrap or non-null assertion is fine: a panicking test is a failing test.\\n4. **Every acquired resource is released on every path** — via the language's scoped construct (`with`, `defer`, RAII, `use`, `try-with-resources`), not cleanup at the end of the happy path.\\n5. **No secret in source, config, fixture or log; no participant data in a log.** See §12.\\n6. **Generated and vendored code is never hand-edited.** Fix the source or the schema and regenerate; upgrade the package. Each language file lists the paths.\\n7. **Never make CI green by removing the signal** — no skipped or deleted failing test, no disabled lint, no widened type, no loosened assertion. Fix the cause, or stop and say what is failing.\\n8. **Never invent an API.** Verify that a function, flag or package exists in the version the repo pins before using it. A new dependency touches the lockfile and is stated in the PR.\\n9. **No stub presented as done** — no `TODO: implement`, `NotImplemented`, hardcoded return, or mock left in a code path described as working. The PR says what is unfinished.\\n10. **Rules bind new and touched code, not the estate.** Do not restyle a file in passing; do not add to its debt. The diff contains only what the change needed.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Types are the cheapest documentation we have\\n\\n**Type it as strongly as the language allows.** Not for the compiler — for the reader, human or agent, landing cold: the signature should say what a function takes and returns without reading the body or chasing call sites.\\n\\n- **Push types outward to the boundary.** Parse and validate untrusted input (HTTP body, device payload, env var, file) *once*, at the edge, into a typed value. Inside the boundary, trust the types. \\\"Parse, don't validate.\\\"\\n- **Name the domain, don't reuse the primitive.** Three `string` parameters in a row will be called in the wrong order. A `DeviceId`/`SessionId` newtype or branded type costs a line and removes the class of error — especially for what we pass everywhere: device serials, session ids, timestamps, units.\\n- **Make illegal states unrepresentable.** A discriminated union or sealed class beats a struct with four nullable fields and an implied rule.\\n- **A type that lies is worse than no type.** A cast that makes the build pass converts a compile-time failure into a runtime one.\\n\\n## 2. Functional by default\\n\\n**In every language that supports it:** declarative over imperative, values over mutation, composition over inheritance, and the language's own algorithm library over a loop you wrote. The imperative version is always available; it carries the burden of justification.\\n\\n- **Say what, not how.** `filter → map → fold` over an index loop with an accumulator.\\n- **Reuse the built-in algorithm** — it is already correct and already optimised; a hand-rolled one is a fresh bug surface. Each language file names the library.\\n- **Pure by default.** Inputs to outputs; no hidden reads, no mutated arguments, no I/O. Effects go to the edges (§7).\\n- **Name a non-trivial lambda.** A fifteen-line anonymous closure is worse than the loop it replaced.\\n- **Use the language's own monadic vocabulary** for the failure path (`Option`/`Result`, `?.`/`??`, `optional`/`expected`, narrowed `T | None`) instead of nested null checks and try/catch pyramids — and **do not smuggle in what the language does not have.** A hand-built monad library is a private dialect nobody else can review.\\n\\n**Where the paradigm stops:**\\n\\n- **Known allocation-sensitive contexts — Unity `Update`/`FixedUpdate`/`LateUpdate`, per-sample DSP callbacks, ISRs, the kernel data path, a render loop.** There, preallocated imperative code is the default and needs no measurement. Everywhere else, an imperative rewrite for performance needs a profile, stated in the commit.\\n- **A language that does not idiomatically support it** — C, Bash, kernel code, Go. The residue still pays: pure helpers, no hidden global state, the standard library over hand-rolling.\\n\\n## 3. Names\\n\\nEvery fact in a name never goes stale, never costs a separate read, and cannot contradict the code.\\n\\n- Name after **what it means in the domain**, not what it is technically. `sessionsAwaitingUpload`, not `list2` or `sessionArray`.\\n- **Omit needless words.** Strip what the type already says (`sensorList`, `configObject`), the empty role-nouns (`Manager`, `Helper`, `Utils`, `Handler`, `Info`, `Impl`), and verbs that do no work (`doCalculate`). Error types keep the ecosystem's suffix (`Error`, `Exception`); spend the words before it on what went wrong — `SessionAlreadyClosedError`, not `SessionError`.\\n- **Don't stack words like bricks.** A name needing five words is usually a thing doing five things.\\n- **Strongly avoid single-letter names.** Three carve-outs: a loop index or coordinate in a small scope; a mathematical or signal-processing symbol where the surrounding code is written in that vocabulary (`n`, `fs`, `x[n]`); Go method receivers.\\n- **No code names or metaphors in identifiers.** A module called `Poseidon` costs every reader a lookup forever.\\n- **Booleans read as assertions** — `isConnected`, `hasConsent`. Never negated (`notReady`).\\n- **Same concept, same word, everywhere.** Pick `device` or `headset` and hold the line; the domain's settled terms live in [`domain-modeling`](../../../vendor/mattpocock/skills/skills/engineering/domain-modeling/SKILL.md).\\n- **Don't stutter.** `Condition.isTrue()`, not `Condition.checkCondition()`; `session.New()`, not `session.NewSession()`.\\n- **Accessors are nouns where the language leaves it open** — `count()` not `getCount()` in Rust, Go (Effective Go mandates it) and C++ (Google's guide: accessors are named like variables). Keep the binding convention where one exists: JavaBean accessors, C# properties, Kotlin `val`.\\n- **Units in the name or the type** — `timeout_s`, `window_ms`, `sample_rate_hz`, `amplitude_uv`. A bare `duration` in signal code is a defect.\\n\\n### Arguments: fewer first, then named\\n\\n- **Reduce the count before improving the names.** Three parameters that always travel together are a type.\\n- **A boolean parameter is usually two functions.** `render(data, true)` means the function does two things and the caller picks. Where the flag genuinely is data, a two-value enum names both states at the call site.\\n- **Once a call takes more than one primitive or boolean, name them at the call site:** keyword-only args (Python, `*`), named arguments (C#, Kotlin), an options object (TS), a parameter struct or builder (Rust, Go, Java), a designated-initializer struct (C, C++) — or, only where you do not control the signature, the `/* name= */` comment.\\n\\n## 4. Modules and boundaries\\n\\nThe highest-leverage quality property, and the one AI-generated code most often gets wrong — it produces *many shallow* modules where a few deep ones belong.\\n\\n- **Deep over shallow.** A module worth having hides substantially more complexity than its interface exposes. A wrapper as wide as its implementation bought nothing. Vocabulary: the vendored [`codebase-design`](../../../vendor/mattpocock/skills/skills/engineering/codebase-design/SKILL.md) skill.\\n- **Put the seam where the change will come** — a second transport, a second storage backend. An abstraction over a change that never comes is pure cost.\\n- **One reason to change per module.** A file edited by both \\\"the UI changed\\\" and \\\"the wire protocol changed\\\" is two modules.\\n- **Dependencies point one way.** Domain logic does not import transport, UI or persistence — otherwise it cannot be tested without them.\\n- **Law of Demeter.** `session.device().radio().config().rate` couples the caller to three types it should not know. Ask the object you hold for what you need.\\n- **Composition over inheritance.** Inheritance is the tightest coupling available; open a type for subclassing only when that is the design.\\n- **Count the nouns.** When `String`, `List`, `Map`, `dict` and `id` dominate over `session`, `device`, `channel`, `sample`, the domain is modelled in primitives and every rule about it lives in the callers.\\n- **Resist premature extraction.** Two similar call sites are a coincidence; three are a pattern.\\n- **No vague buckets** — `util`, `utils`, `common`, `helpers`, `misc`, `shared`, `base`, `core` as a file, folder or package name. They attract everything, inform nobody, become dependency sinks and hide the type the three functions inside should have been. Name the container for what is in it (`sample-window`, `network-retry`); if no name fits, the things do not belong together. New code does not add to an existing bucket.\\n\\n### Small outside, free to be larger inside\\n\\n**Prefer small** — files, types, functions, interfaces — because a reader holds a handful of ideas at once, and at every level a component should be understandable in terms of a small number of well-named parts. **Prefer deep** because a module's value is hidden complexity over exposed interface. These agree about interfaces and contest only implementations, so: **a deep module is small on the outside and free to be larger on the inside.** Split a function that is a sequence of named steps; do not split a coherent implementation into ten files to make each short. Ten one-line wrappers are worse than one clear twenty-line function — that is shallow-module proliferation wearing smallness as a disguise, and it is the failure AI-generated code falls into.\\n\\n**Start simple.** Complexity arrives in answer to a real requirement or a measured problem, never in anticipation of one.\\n\\n## 5. Errors and failure\\n\\n- **Fail fast at the boundary, degrade gracefully at the top.** Reject bad input where it arrives, naming what was wrong. Decide how to survive it once, at a level that can decide.\\n- **Errors carry context** — which device, session, file, upstream call. Never `throw new Error('failed')`.\\n- **Distinguish expected from exceptional.** \\\"Device not connected\\\" is a normal state and belongs in the return type. \\\"Disk is corrupt\\\" is exceptional.\\n- **Retries need a bound and a backoff**, and only wrap idempotent operations.\\n- **Bound every queue, buffer and batch**, and decide what happens when it fills — block, drop oldest, drop newest, fail. For a sensor stream, drop with a counter and a metric; never drop silently.\\n\\n## 6. Output: the data plane and the control plane\\n\\n- **stdout is the data plane** — the output a caller consumes or parses, with a stable documented shape, and *nothing else on it*. One stray progress line silently corrupts whatever is downstream.\\n- **stderr is the control plane** — logs, progress, warnings, everything *about* the run. Also where all output goes when the program has no data plane, which is the common case: services, daemons, device tools that only perform an action.\\n- **Print is not a logger.** `print`, `console.log`, `println!`, `fmt.Println`, `echo` all default to stdout. Diagnostics go through the language's logging facility, which goes to stderr and can be turned off.\\n- **Configure the log format once, centrally** — timestamp, level, source, message, plus ambient context (request/device/session id) bound to the logger or scope, never pasted into every message. A per-module logger gives the source for free.\\n- **Levels mean what the reader must do.** `error`: someone must act. `warn`: someone should look. `info`: normal operation worth narrating. `debug`: only when diagnosing. A line nobody will act on hides the one that matters.\\n- **Structured (key/value or JSON) where anything will aggregate the logs**; human-readable for a local CLI or device script.\\n\\nAndroid, Unity, the kernel and the browser have no usable stdout; the principle holds — data out through the API, diagnostics through the platform's log channel — and the language files name the channel.\\n\\n## 7. State, mutation and time\\n\\n- **Immutable by default.** `const`/`val`/`final`/frozen. Relax only where mutation is the point (a hot loop, a buffer).\\n- **Never hand back a mutable internal.** Returning the live `List` or array is a private field with extra syntax. Return a read-only view, a copy, or a method that does what the caller wanted.\\n- **No hidden global state.** Module-level mutable singletons make tests order-dependent. Pass dependencies in.\\n- **Pure core, effectful shell.** Inject the clock, the filesystem, randomness and the network. `now: datetime` as a parameter is the difference between a test and a flake.\\n\\n**Time bites us harder than most** — timestamped biometric samples cross headset → gateway → time-series store:\\n\\n- **Monotonic clock for durations, wall clock for timestamps.** `time.monotonic()`, `Instant`, `steady_clock`, `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()`, `performance.now()`.\\n- **Store and transmit UTC** with an explicit offset or `Z`; convert to local only for display.\\n- **Device time is not cloud time.** Record which clock a timestamp came from; never join two clocks without reconciling. Silent mixing surfaces as an unexplained gap in a session months later.\\n\\n## 8. Testability and tests\\n\\n- **Hard to test is information about the design.** Reach for a better seam before a heavier mock.\\n- **Test behaviour, not implementation.** A test that breaks on every refactor is a tax; one that passes while behaviour breaks is a lie.\\n- **Failure modes first** — empty, malformed, timeout, disconnection, concurrent second call. The happy path is the one manual use finds anyway.\\n- **Deterministic or delete it.** No sleeps as synchronisation, no real network or hardware, no test-order or wall-clock dependence.\\n- **Name the test after the claim** — `rejects_a_session_with_no_consent`, not `test3`.\\n- **Prefer a real implementation or an in-memory fake over a mock with five expectations.**\\n- **Signal processing gets a synthetic input with a known answer** — a pure sine at a known frequency, a known artefact — never golden-output pinning.\\n\\n## 9. Concision and clarity\\n\\nConcise means *less to read*, not fewer characters.\\n\\n- **Delete rather than comment out.** Git remembers.\\n- **Guard clauses over nested conditionals.** Keep the main path at the left margin.\\n- **Keep cognitive complexity low, and let the linter measure it** (`C901`, `readability-function-cognitive-complexity`, detekt, ESLint `complexity`).\\n- **Extract a function when you would otherwise write a comment explaining the next ten lines** — the name is the comment and stays true. Apply the §4 test: extract a *sequence of named steps*; do not shatter a coherent implementation into one-line wrappers.\\n- **Kill the cleverness.** A dense one-liner that takes three reads is not concise.\\n- **Do not build what you were not asked for.** Speculative options, flags and extension points are the commonest form of AI over-delivery.\\n\\n## 10. Comments and documentation\\n\\nA comment is a cost to justify: nothing checks it, so a stale one misinforms; a correct one is still attention spent; and the further a description sits from the code, the faster it rots unnoticed. Express a fact as far up this list as you can:\\n\\n| Form | Checked by | How it fails |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Types and signatures | the compiler, every build | cannot go stale |\\n| Tests | every CI run | goes red |\\n| Names | every reader | drifts, in plain sight |\\n| Inline and doc comments | nothing | quietly |\\n| Repo docs and diagrams | nothing | fastest, least visibly |\\n\\nSo the first three moves are **rename**, **extract**, or **introduce a type**. Comments that survive explain **why**, never what. They earn their place for: a **workaround** (what is broken, whose bug, **link the ticket**); a **regex** (intent plus a matching and a non-matching example); a **gap in the language** (`/* blocking= */ true` in C++); a **non-local invariant**; a **hardware or platform quirk** (\\\"one bind per boot — a second call crashes the HAL\\\"); a **measured performance decision**, with the number; a **deliberate omission** — an ignored error, a suppressed lint, an empty branch.\\n\\n**Public API doc comments are a different artefact** — the contract for someone who will never open the body (the Pegasus SDK `API` surface, `evt-demo-core`, shared `libs/`): what it does, assumes, throws, and its units and ranges. **High-level architecture docs earn their place** because the alternative is reading the whole codebase; keeping them current is real work an agent is good at. **A stale comment is a bug** — fix it in the same diff, and keep `README`/`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` true, since that is the first thing the next agent reads.\\n\\n## 11. Efficiency, honestly\\n\\n- **Correct, clear, then fast — and fast only when measured**, outside the known hot paths named in §2.\\n- **Know the order of magnitude.** An accidental O(n²) over a session's samples, or a query in a loop, is a design defect regardless of profiling.\\n- **Costs live at the boundaries** — I/O, serialisation, allocation in a loop, round-trips. Batch, stream, do not load a whole recording to read its header.\\n- **State the measurement in the commit** when a change is made for performance, or the next reader will \\\"simplify\\\" it back.\\n\\n## 12. Dependencies, security and participant data\\n\\n- **Reuse what exists here first** — search the repo and the sibling repos before writing a helper.\\n- **A new dependency is a decision with a cost** — supply chain, licence, upgrade burden, bundle size. Small, maintained, pinned; anything load-bearing gets an ADR.\\n- **Validate at every trust boundary** — HTTP handlers, device payloads, file parsers, CLI arguments, IPC, and **query text**: a request value never enters a Flux/SQL string by interpolation.\\n- **Configuration is injected and validated at startup.** No hardcoded endpoints, ARNs, buckets, ports. Parse config once into a typed object and **fail at boot**, not on the first request that needs the missing value.\\n\\n**Participant data.** We hold biometric signals and metadata from human research participants.\\n\\n- **The identifier that travels is the pseudonymous session/device id.** Names, contact details and anything that re-identifies a participant live only in the consent/enrolment store, never in signal payloads, file names, logs, metrics labels, bug reports or test fixtures.\\n- **Signal data is sensitive by default** — EEG/ECG/PPG payloads are treated as identifying even when no name is attached. Encrypted at rest on device and in the cloud; never copied to a laptop or a shared drive outside the documented data path.\\n- **Retention outlives code.** Before a migration drops, renames or reinterprets a field that holds study data, check the study's retention and consent constraints — §13 — and get it confirmed, not assumed.\\n- **Real recordings are not test fixtures.** Tests use synthetic signals or an approved de-identified dataset.\\n\\n## 13. Contracts and compatibility\\n\\nA **contract** is any interface you cannot change unilaterally because the two sides deploy separately — a headset in the field runs firmware from months ago while the cloud ships weekly: a published API, a wire format, a persisted schema, a file layout, a CLI's stdout.\\n\\n**No change may require both sides to deploy together.** Every change is expand → migrate → contract: add the new thing tolerated-but-not-required; move writers then readers (or the reverse, whichever is safe); remove the old thing once nothing uses it.\\n\\n- **Protobuf** (`sensor.proto`, device ↔ cloud): never reuse or renumber a tag (mark removed ones `reserved`); additive only, readers ignore unknown fields; never change a field's type or meaning; never promote optional to required or tighten validation on a field in the wild. The `.proto` is the contract; generated code is not (§0.6).\\n- **Persisted schemas** (DynamoDB, Influx, S3 layouts, on-device files): migrations are re-runnable and forward-compatible; the old shape stays readable until every writer has moved.\\n- **Published API surfaces** (Pegasus SDK `API`, `evt-demo-core`, shared `libs/`): semver meant literally; deprecate before removing, with the language's marker **and the replacement named in the message**; never change a public signature or behaviour silently.\\n\\n## 14. Before you call it done\\n\\n- The formatter and linter for the language have run and pass; where none is configured, the PR says so.\\n- The tests you added fail without your change.\\n- The unhappy paths have somewhere to go.\\n- No `TODO` without a ticket key, no debug print, no commented-out block, no unused import or dead branch.\\n- The diff contains only what the change needed.\\n\\n---\\n\\n*Sources worth reading whole:* Kevlin Henney, *Seven Ineffective Coding Habits of Many Programmers* (§3, §10); John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (§4, via `codebase-design`); Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* ch. 3 (the smell baseline `code-review` applies on top of this).\\n\\n===== /Users/yuratestdev/.claude/plugins/cache/evolve/evolve-skills/0.1.0/skills/code-standards/languages/python.md =====\\n# Python\\n\\n**Canonical standard:** [PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/), [PEP 257](https://peps.python.org/pep-0257/) for docstrings, [PEP 484/585/604](https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/) for typing. We do not maintain a private Python style guide.\\n\\n**Tooling is authoritative:** [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) — `ruff format` (Black-compatible) and `ruff check --fix`. This is the house config for every Python project; **no project has it yet** — `signal-quality/pyproject.toml` selects only `E, F, I, UP`, `research-development` has no `[tool.ruff]` at all, and nothing runs ruff or a type checker in CI. The first Python PR in a repo adds this block and a CI step:\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.ruff]\\nline-length = 88\\ntarget-version = \\\"py312\\\"\\n\\n[tool.ruff.lint]\\nselect = [\\\"E\\\", \\\"F\\\", \\\"I\\\", \\\"UP\\\", \\\"B\\\", \\\"SIM\\\", \\\"ANN\\\", \\\"D\\\", \\\"C90\\\", \\\"RUF\\\"]\\n\\n[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]\\nconvention = \\\"google\\\"\\n```\\n\\n(`E`/`F` pycodestyle+pyflakes, `I` import order, `UP` modernisation, `B` bugbear, `SIM` simplification, `ANN` missing annotations, `D` docstrings in the Google format, `C90` McCabe complexity, `RUF` Ruff's own.) The type-hint, docstring-format and complexity rules below are each enforced by this config, which is why they can be short here.\\n\\n**Where we write it:** `research-development` (MNE/NumPy/SciPy analysis, Python 3.12) · `evolve-device-manager/.../signal-quality` (live LSL signal-quality pipelines, pinned 3.12) · `evolve-lsl-protocols` · `ai-core/skills/*/scripts` · `datasets`. Environments are `uv`-managed where a `pyproject.toml` exists.\\n\\n## Non-negotiables\\n\\n- **Type hints on every function signature.** Parameters and return, including `-> None`. This is the house rule the team cares most about — a signature that states its types is readable cold, by a person or an agent, without reading the body. Locals may rely on inference.\\n- **Modern syntax:** `list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, `X | None` — not `List`, `Dict`, `Optional[X]`. `from __future__ import annotations` where a runtime needs it.\\n- **Never a bare `except:`**, and never `except Exception: pass`. Catch the narrowest exception that can actually occur, add context, and re-raise or handle. `raise ... from err` preserves the chain.\\n- **`pathlib.Path`, not `os.path`** string juggling. We run on Windows and Linux; string paths are where that breaks.\\n- **Context managers for every resource** — files, sockets, LSL inlets, subprocess pipes, DB handles.\\n- **No mutable default arguments** (`def f(xs: list[int] = [])`). Bugbear catches this; it still gets written.\\n- **`logging`, not `print`.** `print` writes to **stdout**, which is the data plane — a stray debug print corrupts whatever is parsing the output. Diagnostics go through `logging`, which writes to stderr. `print` is correct only when the thing being printed *is* the program's output. See §6 of [universal.md](../reference/universal.md).\\n- **Dataclasses over dict-shaped data.** `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` for a value; a `dict[str, Any]` passed between functions is an untyped record and every field access is a guess.\\n- **`if __name__ == \\\"__main__\\\":`** guards every script, with the work in a function so it can be imported and tested.\\n- **Force keyword arguments where a call could be misread.** A bare `*` in the signature makes every parameter after it keyword-only, so the call site names them and cannot silently reorder them:\\n\\n  ```python\\n  def start_stream(device: DeviceId, *, blocking: bool, timeout_s: float) -> Stream: ...\\n\\n  start_stream(device, blocking=True, timeout_s=2.0)   # the only legal call\\n  ```\\n\\n  Use it for any function taking more than one primitive or boolean parameter — see §3 of [universal.md](../reference/universal.md). It is also the cheapest API-stability tool Python has: keyword-only parameters can be reordered or added without breaking a caller.\\n- **f-strings** for interpolation; `%`-style only inside `logger` calls, where deferred formatting is the point.\\n\\n## House deltas\\n\\n| Rule | Why we differ |\\n|---|---|\\n| Type hints are **mandatory** on function signatures, not optional as PEP 484 allows | Comprehension by humans and AI agents. An unannotated signature forces a reader to reconstruct the contract from the body and the call sites; the annotation is a fraction of the cost and never goes stale silently. |\\n| Docstrings required on public modules, classes and functions; **Google style** (`Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:`) | PEP 257 does not pick a format. Picking one makes them parseable and stops per-file drift. Private helpers whose name and signature already say everything do not need one. |\\n| No `Any` in a signature without a comment saying why | `Any` in a signature is an unannotated function wearing a disguise. |\\n| Units go in the name or the type | We pass a lot of physical quantities. `timeout_s`, `window_ms`, `amplitude_uv` — a bare `duration` has caused real bugs. |\\n\\n## Where we differ from Google's Python guide\\n\\n[Google's Python guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html) is a good companion to PEP 8 and we follow it on naming, docstring format, the `main()`/`__name__` rule, the ban on bare `except`, power features, and the comprehension limit above. Four deliberate divergences:\\n\\n| Google says | We say | Why |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| \\\"Use `import` statements for packages and modules only, not for individual types, classes, or functions\\\" | Import names freely — `from pathlib import Path`, `from typing import Sequence` | PEP 8 does not require module-only imports and the wider ecosystem does not follow this one; it is the most widely-ignored rule in Google's guide, our code does not follow it, and `pathlib.Path` written out everywhere is worse, not better. |\\n| Line length 80 | 88 | Ruff/Black's default, already configured in `signal-quality/pyproject.toml`. Rung 2 of the ladder — the config is enforced, this file is not. |\\n| Type annotations optional; \\\"at least annotate your public APIs\\\" | Mandatory on every function signature | The house typing rule. See §1 of [universal.md](../reference/universal.md). |\\n| Type-check with `pytype` | `mypy --strict` or `pyright` | `pytype` is effectively Google-internal; mypy and pyright are what the ecosystem and our editors use. |\\n\\n## Typing depth\\n\\n- **Type-check in CI where the project supports it** — `mypy --strict` or `pyright`. Ruff's `ANN` rules catch *missing* annotations; only a type checker catches *wrong* ones.\\n- Use `typing.NewType` for identifiers that must not be interchangeable (`SessionId = NewType(\\\"SessionId\\\", str)`).\\n- `Protocol` for structural interfaces — it is what makes a fake injectable without a base class.\\n- `Literal` and `enum.Enum` instead of magic strings for a closed set of options.\\n- Annotate NumPy arrays as precisely as the project allows (`npt.NDArray[np.float64]`), and **write the expected shape in the docstring** — `(n_channels, n_samples)`. Shape is the type information NumPy cannot carry, and shape mismatches are our most common analysis bug.\\n\\n## Logging\\n\\n- **One module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`** per module, and nothing else. `__name__` is the source origin, for free and always correct — never write the module name into the message.\\n- **Configure once, at the entry point**, with `logging.dictConfig` (or `basicConfig` for a small script): the format string carries `%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s` plus the message, and the level comes from a flag or an env var. Libraries and modules configure nothing — they only ever call `getLogger` and log.\\n- **Lazy `%s` args, never an f-string:** `logger.debug(\\\"dropped %d samples on %s\\\", n, device_id)`. The f-string version formats even when the level is off, and it destroys the message template that structured handlers and log aggregation group on.\\n- **`logger.exception(...)` inside an `except` block** — it attaches the traceback. `logger.error(str(e))` throws away the only part that helps.\\n- Ambient context (device id, session id) goes on a `LoggerAdapter`, a filter, or `extra=` — configured once for the run, not pasted into every message.\\n- Structured JSON output for anything that will be aggregated; the default human-readable format is right for local scripts and analysis code.\\n\\n## Functional style\\n\\nPython's functional idiom is the comprehension and the standard library, not a transplanted Haskell.\\n\\n- **Comprehensions and generator expressions over accumulator loops.** `[transform(s) for s in samples if is_valid(s)]` says what; a `for` loop with `result.append()` says how. PEP 8's own preference is a comprehension over `map`/`filter` with a lambda — follow it. **One comprehension, one `for` clause** (Google's rule): a nested or multi-filter comprehension is denser than the loop it replaced, so unroll it.\\n- **Generators for anything streaming.** `yield` a session's samples rather than materialising a list; it composes and it does not hold a recording in memory.\\n- **`itertools` and `functools` before writing it yourself** — `chain`, `islice`, `groupby`, `pairwise`, `batched` (3.12), `accumulate`, `partial`, `cache`, `singledispatch`. Every one is C-speed and already correct. `functools.reduce` is the exception: it is usually less readable than a loop or `sum`/`math.prod`, so use it sparingly.\\n- **Pure functions, immutable values.** `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` for records, `tuple` over `list` for fixed collections, and never mutate an argument unless the name says so.\\n- **NumPy is the declarative form in numeric code.** A vectorised expression *is* the pipeline — see the next section; it is the same principle with a different algorithm library.\\n- **Don't smuggle in monads.** Python has no `Result` type and no do-notation. The idiomatic failure vocabulary is `T | None` with narrowing, and exceptions for the exceptional. A hand-rolled `Either` class is a private dialect.\\n\\n## Scientific and signal-processing code\\n\\nThis is most of our Python, and it has its own failure modes:\\n\\n- **Vectorise.** A per-sample Python loop over a recording is orders of magnitude off; use NumPy/SciPy operations. This is not micro-optimisation — it is the difference between seconds and hours on a session.\\n- **State the units and the sample rate at the boundary**, and convert once. Never let µV/V or ms/s ambiguity travel through a pipeline.\\n- **Do not mutate an input array** unless the function's name says so; copy or return new.\\n- **Seed every random operation** used in an analysis, and log the seed. An unreproducible result is not a result.\\n- **Separate the pipeline from the plotting.** A function that computes and also draws cannot be tested or reused.\\n- Guard against NaN/inf explicitly at the point they can enter (bad channel, dropped packet); do not let them propagate into a metric that silently becomes `nan`.\\n\\n## Testing\\n\\n`pytest`, in `tests/`, named `test_*.py`.\\n\\n- Plain `assert`; `pytest.raises` for the failure cases; `pytest.approx` for floats — never `==` on a float.\\n- Fixtures for setup, `tmp_path` for filesystem work, `monkeypatch` for environment.\\n- `@pytest.mark.parametrize` instead of a loop inside one test, so a failure names the case.\\n- Signal-processing functions get a **synthetic input with a known answer** (a pure sine at a known frequency, a known artefact) — that is the only way to test a transform without pinning it to its own output.\\n- Tests must not need hardware, a network, or a real LSL stream. Put the device behind a `Protocol` and pass a fake.\"}}\n",
